note: The replica dossier repeatedly pins the unified marker to exactly three legitimate setters (no-command entrypoint, compose one-shot, self-host ephemeral-run), matching the decision doc and the blob-config gate's own error text verbatim. The conformance blob-backend runner's os.Setenv(...,"unified") is an unauthorized fourth setter with no dossier or design-corpus sanction — the code is the drifted side, not the doc. Queue fix-code: either drop the conformance tool's use of the marker or give it a real, doc-acknowledged reason to exist.

The node-subscription dossier explicitly names this exact defect and its own resolution: "messages.* auto-subscribe edge injection surviving the June-18 coverage-check unification — adjudicated: the injection code is the drifted side, remove it (fix-code, finding 1312)" (transcript tier, 2026-07-13). The decision doc's claim that substitution refs do not contribute edges is CURRENT intent; the code's edgeFromMessageRef feeder is the leftover that must be removed. Doc left unedited; this row duplicates already-adjudicated finding 1312.

User ruling 2026-07-17 (design-call resolved, option A): the reconciler's 'with backoff' clause was dossier/decision distillation drift — its sole artifact source evidences only the no-attempt-cap property. The flat fixed-interval retry-forever behavior is ratified as intent; per-row backoff is explicitly not required (revisit only with real outage evidence). 'With backoff' dropped from publisher-subscription.md, decision:subscription-reconciler, and both dossier entries. Supersedes this row's earlier fix-code queueing — no code change; the doc side was the defect.

The attribute and node-run dossiers confirm non-cascade creations (operator_invalidate, recalculate, message_delivery) copy the prior run's bag verbatim at creation with no substitution round there; the only substitution that can fail for such a row is the claim-substitution round at dispatch (stale->running), which runner.go's applyAttributeFailure handles by opening a fresh transaction distinct from the row-creation transaction. The decision doc's claim that non-cascade failures route in the row-creation transaction is wrong. Edited the doc's Choice section to describe the fresh dispatch-time transaction for non-cascade rows.

The attribute dossier ties template_resolution_failed specifically to the missing-source case ("only a required strict ref with no fallback escalates to template_resolution_failed"). Code confirms classifyAttributeFailure maps attributeValidationError (schema-validation failures) to the distinct template_validation_failed class; only ErrMissingSource and the untyped catch-all map to template_resolution_failed. The doc's claim that schema-validation failures also route to template_resolution_failed is wrong. Edited the doc's Choice section (same edit as 2292) to state the two distinct classes.

The node-subscription dossier states unambiguously (transcript tier, 2026-06-16/17): "event/<name> subscription type-paths and {{nodes.X.event.Y}} substitution — retired with named events; replacement is terminal/* + CEL tag filters." "Event reads" is a retired substitution-grammar shape and no longer belongs in the coverage doc's enumeration. Edited the doc's Choice section to drop the phrase; coverage now reads "per-field attribute reads and whole-pull reads."

Same underlying drift as 1314 (retired event-read substitution form still named in the coverage doc), corroborated identically by the node-subscription dossier's retirement record. Single edit applied to the doc covers both rows.

CreateInstanceWithServiceBindings carries the same @decision annotation as CreateInstanceWithOverrides and performs the identical wake POST, but omits the waitForRootDispatch call that CreateInstanceWithOverrides makes right after waking (harness.go:434-435 vs :541 with no wait). The instance dossier confirms the wake-after-create sweep was meant to apply everywhere ("swept everywhere", 2026-06-16 transcript); this helper only got half of it. The decision doc's own wording (uniform wait-for-root-dispatch semantics across create-instance helpers) is correct design intent; the harness code is the drifted side. Queue fix-test to add the missing wait call.

The executor dossier's Required behaviors describe all three deadlines as per-node with plain numeric defaults (sync_rpc_deadline 30s, max_quiet_period 0, max_runtime 0), never as an executor-declared layer. Code confirms: all three are TemplateNodeDef per-node fields; resolve* helpers take (node, deploymentDefault) with no executor-scoped declaration anywhere in spec/ or config/. The doc's "executor-template-level" labeling for two of the three deadlines is wrong. Edited the doc's Choice list to per-node uniformly and added a clarifying line that there is no separate executor-level declaration layer.

The node-subscription dossier states plainly: "force_upstream_refresh is the only cascade flag of its kind" and separately records wake_on_change's full removal (transcript tier, 2026-06-23/24). Code confirms the emitted suggested_subscribes_entry carries exactly one boolean (force_upstream_refresh); the model has no second flag. The doc's "both flags set to false" phrasing is stale from before the second cascade flag (wake_on_change) was retired. Edited the doc's Choice section to name the single flag.
Same underlying drift as 1360 (stale two-flag phrasing after wake_on_change's removal), corroborated identically by the node-subscription dossier. Single edit applied to the doc covers both rows.

The error-policy dossier's Net position lists the validator's range-check union as four groups — executor-declared classes, the acquire/* family, runtime-synthesized classes, and producer-declared classes — calling out runtime-synthesized classes as distinct from acquire/*. Code confirms isRuntimeSynthesizedErrorClass accepts acquire/* plus six named non-acquire classes (template_resolution_failed, template_validation_failed, executor_schema_unavailable, attributes_schema_failed, retry_loop_no_progress, unresolved_executor). The doc's three-group enumeration omits this fourth group. Edited the doc's Choice section to add it.
